newsitem.title: PERU: Peruvian guerrillas switch from ultimatum to appeal.
newsitem.headline: Peruvian guerrillas switch from ultimatum to appeal.

text.p: The Marxist guerrillas holding the residence of Japan's ambassador in Lima have switched from ultimatum to appeal in successive communiques setting out their terms for releasing remaining hostages seized in a spectacular raid on Dec. 17.

The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels issued their first public statement three days after seizing the residence. It demanded the release of some 400 Tupac Amaru members held in different prisons in Peru and was couched in unambiguous language:
"The only possible solution is to listen to our requests and proceed with the freedom of all our jailed members."
Two days later, the guerrillas released 225 hostages and issued their second statement.
"The ... freedom of the authorities that today remain prisoners (inside the residence) will only be possible if the government frees our comrades," it said.

On Christmas Eve, however, the hostage takers released Uruguay's ambassador, Tabare Bocalondro, apparently in response to his government's decision to set free two MRTA leaders held in a Uruguayan jail.

A Japanese diplomat, Kenji Hirata, was next to be freed, for health reasons, followed by Guatemalan Ambassador Jose Maria Argueta in a gesture the guerrillas said was taken to recognize his government's efforts to conclude a peace accord with Guatemalan guerrillas.
The Tupac Amaru issued their third, and so far last, communique after Saturday's release of 20 additional hostages at the end of a face-to-face meeting with government negotiator Domingo Palermo.

Amounting to a plea for understanding the guerrillas' motives, the statement differed markedly in tone from previous communications and dropped the original demand for a tit-for-tat release of hostages in exchange for prisoners.

It said: "We reiterate our willingness to solve through dialogue our withdrawal from the occupied residence. For (this) it is important to reflect why this extreme situation arose in the first place and the drama through which the families of our jailed comrades have lived for years.

"We think this will allow it to be understood that our request (for freeing imprisoned members) should be attended to and thus permit in the long run a global and lasting peace. We will play a responsible role in that effort."
The communique was signed by Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, who led the assault on the residence.
In an interview from Hamburg, Germany, MRTA spokesman Isaac Velazco went a step further, saying the rebels would consider "an intermediate solution."
"We still insist on the liberation of the politcal prisoners but we consider that an intermediate solution can be reached."
